subject: Geopolitics
title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
description: A short lesson to help you apply Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

hook.text: In 1968 the world made a bargain: five nations keep nukes, the rest don't. Four nations broke the deal.

buildup.text: The NPT recognized the US, Russia, UK, France, and China as nuclear states. Everyone else pledged to stay non-nuclear.

discovery.text: In exchange, nuclear states promised to disarm eventually. Over 50 years later, they haven't. Trust eroded.

twist.text: India, Pakistan, Israel, and North Korea all got nukes outside the NPT. The treaty couldn't stop determined actors.

climax.text: The NPT slowed proliferation but didn't stop it. Without it, experts say 30 nations might have gone nuclear.

punchline.text: An imperfect treaty beats no treaty at all.

quiz.question: Which nations went nuclear outside the NPT framework?
